title: LatticeBridge connector + reseller pilot framing
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood AE/SE and LatticeBridge partnership team to explore a reseller + connector pilot for hybrid GPU capacity. Covered architecture fit, security/compliance gates, pilot success metrics, and next steps (pilot scope, benchmarks, NDA/SLA asks).
topics: business model fit: reseller vs managed connector
technical constraints: network, VPC, KV cache, routing
security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO
pilot framing: benchmarks, timeline, pricing model
integration touchpoints: SDKs, routing policies, autoscale
action_items: Alex Chen; Send pilot one-pager + initial pricing bands; due 2026-10-22
Priya Kapoor; Share sample benchmark harness and guidance for KV cache metrics; due 2026-10-26
Nina Park; Send list of LatticeBridge customer verticals and target pilot accounts; due 2026-10-23
Omar Santos; Provide network topology and firewall constraints for VPC peering; due 2026-10-25
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot SOW template and pricing ranges
Schedule technical kickoff with infra/DevEx (week of 10/26)
Agree on two benchmark prompts and target latency/cost SLOs
NDA amendment for reseller revenue share (legal)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-19 15:30 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marcus Holt (Redwood Solutions), Nina Park (LatticeBridge VP Partnerships), Omar Santos (LatticeBridge Cloud Ops), Jules Carter (Product), Diego Ramos (Sales)

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros, we are Redwood Inference, I run partnerships and channel for the US.
00:12 Nina Park: Hi hi, Nina here. We do channel + connector work for hybrid GPU access for systems integrators and cloud resellers. Glad to chat, there's a lot of overlap.
00:23 Priya Kapoor: Thanks — quick from our side I'm Priya, SE — I'll focus on the technical fit and pilot plan. Marcus will help scope the reseller ops.
00:35 Diego Ramos: Quick q — what's the typical revenue share for your reseller programs, or is that negotiable per deal?
00:44 Alex Chen: We usually have tiered bands, depends on committed capacity — we'll send ranges after this call; pilot deals usually have special introductory margins.
00:52 Jules Carter: From product perspective we care about latency profiles and whether we can route to on-prem GPUs dynamically, not always toss everything to the hosted API.
01:07 Priya Kapoor: Right, that maps well — Redwood has hosted, dedicated, and private. For a connector/reseller workflow folks commonly use our connector to route customer traffic either to Redwood hosted or to a customer-managed pool. We also support VPC peering and an on-prem package for air-gapped customers.
01:28 Omar Santos: On the VPC peering, for our customers the firewall stance is fairly strict — no inbound ports, we prefer outbound-only tunnels and a connector agent. Is that supported?
01:42 Priya Kapoor: Yes, we can do outbound-only connectors and we also offer a private control plane option where customer maintains networking. There might be some extra ops for high-throughput KV cache sync across the agent, but we've implemented async replication in other partners.
01:58 Nina Park: How do you handle model variants if a customer wants lower cost? Like quantized variants roaming between regions?
02:10 Marcus Holt: We have smart routing policies — model variants, quantization profiles. You can set routing by latency, cost, or tier, and automatic fallback to compat variants if exact model not available.
02:28 Jules Carter: Any requirements on the GPU instance types? A lot of our partners use mixed fleets — A100s and now some new X cards.
02:40 Priya Kapoor: Runtime chooses kernels by model arch and hardware — we support mixed fleets but recommend a small set of validated SKUs for consistent performance. We can run compatibility tests during pilot.
02:55 Diego Ramos: When you say 'compatibility tests', what does that involve?
03:01 Priya Kapoor: Typically we push a small model, then run a suite of prompts across sequence lengths to measure 95th pct latency, throughput, and token cost. We also verify KV cache behavior and continuous batching efficiency. We'll share the harness.
03:18 Nina Park: Security, can you confirm SOC 2 and KMS integration? Our enterprise customers ask for HSM-backed keys and auditability.
03:29 Alex Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and supports KMS integrations including cloud KMS and HSM via KMIP in Private deployments. Audit logs are available per-tenant, and we expose token-level cost/tracing in the console.
03:44 Omar Santos: Is SSO/SAML supported for partner admin access? We need RBAC for reseller accounts and per-customer tenant separation.
03:55 Marcus Holt: Yes SSO and fine-grained RBAC; you can create partner roles with limited view of accounts and per-tenant isolation. For revenue reconciliation we have exportable billing records.
04:12 Jules Carter: A lot of customers will ask about data retention and model training use of logs. Do you train on customer data?
04:20 Alex Chen: No — Redwood does not train models on customer data by default. We have clear data-use policies and retention controls; customers can opt to disable telemetry. We'll surface the security whitepaper after.
04:33 Diego Ramos: Any concerns on throughput if we broker multi-tenant traffic across a single connector?
04:40 Priya Kapoor: Multi-tenant brokers need careful batching config; our intelligence suggests per-tenant batching windows and KV cache scoping. We'll likely recommend per-tenant KV namespaces to avoid cross-tenant cache pollution.
04:58 Nina Park: For the pilot we're thinking: 3 customers, mix of low-latency chat and higher-throughput embedding workloads. Goal is to validate revenue model and ops overhead. Is that feasible in 6-8 weeks?
05:13 Alex Chen: Yes — typical pilot timeline: week 0 agreements and topology, week 1-2 infra setup and smoke tests, week 3 benchmark runs, week 4-6 pilot run and iteration. 6-8 weeks is realistic.
05:31 Omar Santos: Network — we'll send our topology. Also need to set expectations for burst patterns — some customers have spiky loads. How does autoscale behave?
05:40 Priya Kapoor: We support autoscaling with configurable cooldowns and min/max capacity. For bursty workloads we recommend a small warm pool and burst backstop to hosted to avoid failures. That backstop is opt-in.
05:56 Jules Carter: Pricing model — is it usage-based + a margin for reseller? Or fixed commit?
06:05 Alex Chen: Flexible. For resellers we do both usage-based pass-through + a reseller margin or reserved capacity with commit discounts. Initial pilots often use a blended usage band so both sides can evaluate.
06:18 Diego Ramos: Legal — SLA and indemnity lines — we need to check our standard reseller addendum.
06:24 Alex Chen: We'll share our pilot SOW and reseller addendum. Legal can work in parallel.
06:31 Nina Park: On telemetry — can we get token-level mapping so we can reconcile per-customer billing?
06:37 Marcus Holt: Yes, token-level exports and per-route logs. We can set the retention window you need; some enterprise customers ask for 1-2 years for audits.
06:48 Jules Carter: Benchmarks — can we pick two canonical prompts: a 64-token chat and a 1024-token summarization?
06:55 Priya Kapoor: That sounds good. We'll recommend one chat-style prompt and one long-form summarization plus an embedding workload sample. We'll share expected metrics to aim for.
07:07 Omar Santos: Any red flags you typically see with on-prem connectors? Things that trip partners up?
07:15 Priya Kapoor: Common issues: firewall rules blocking health checks, incorrect clock drift causing audit log gaps, and underprovisioned KV namespaces causing cache churn. We provide a checklist and an infra runbook.
07:30 Nina Park: Are you open to a co-branded page and joint webinar post-pilot? That helps our GTM.
07:36 Alex Chen: Absolutely — joint marketing is part of our partner playbook. We can provide assets and a short case study template.
07:44 Diego Ramos: Competitors — our customers ask why choose Redwood vs CloudGiant or OpenHost. What's the quick pitch?
07:53 Marcus Holt: Production-first, predictable economics, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, and strong observability — token-level tracing and rollback for model rollouts.
08:05 Jules Carter: Attribution — for billing flows do you support per-customer invoicing or only consolidated partner billing?
08:13 Alex Chen: We support both — partners can either resell and consolidate invoices or route billing per-end customer. We'll map to your preferred flow in the SOW.
08:22 Nina Park: Great. On pilot KPIs — propose we track: 95th pct p99 latency target for chat under 300ms for local region, embedding token cost reduction vs baseline, and ops time to onboard < 2 days per customer.
08:36 Alex Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll propose benchmarks and thresholds in the one-pager.
08:44 Priya Kapoor: Next steps for tech: we'll need network topology, a sample model spec (sizes, fp16/quant), and two benchmark prompts. We'll send the harness and an example results sheet.
08:58 Omar Santos: I'll get topology and firewall policy. Also we might need a small NDA tweak for revenue share disclosure.
09:07 Alex Chen: Noted. Legal will follow up.
09:12 Nina Park: Anything else?
09:15 Diego Ramos: Quick note — our early customers will want a pilot discount — will you confirm margins?
09:21 Alex Chen: We'll include that in the ranges we send.
09:25 Marcus Holt: Also linking a short tech doc: redwood.com/partner-connector-runbook (note: internal link shared) and sample harness: github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness (placeholder).
09:41 Alex Chen: Ok let's recap action items.
09:45 Nina Park: Cool, thanks everyone. Looking forward to the docs.
09:48 Alex Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with SOW and pilot plan by Friday.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions flagged — e.g., 'KV cache' typed as 'K-V cash' in one place, 'X cards' label might be vendor shorthand. There was mild crosstalk around 05:30 where Diego and Jules overlapped.

References shared during call: Pilot one-pager (link in chat), Partner runbook (internal link), Benchmark harness (github link placeholder), Legal reseller addendum (to be attached).

Recording ends.
notes: Pilot scope: 3 customers, mix of chat and embedding workloads
Timeline: 6-8 weeks to run pilot with benchmark windows
Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM support, SSO and RBAC available
Ops: recommend per-tenant KV namespaces and outbound-only connector option
